battle.name: 盧旺達內戰
battle.brief: 一九九〇年十月，盧旺達內戰爆發，首都基加利的政治與軍事局勢迅速惡化，政府軍與反政府武裝在盧旺達境內交火。依據戰爭列表，事件歸為「盧旺達內戰」。參戰方使用的惠氏步槍（Winchester Model 1873）正式型號自一八七三年起服役，符合一九九〇年或以前的裝備限制。

kit.name: 惠氏步槍
kit.history: 惠氏步槍是美國早期陸軍採用的制式後膛步槍，以槓桿式重複射擊機構與單排彈倉供彈，主要配給步兵執行一般遠射任務，在栓動步槍普及後逐步退居次要地位。

countries: 這場戰爭於1990年10月1日在盧旺達北部爆發，經過1991年的邊境消耗戰、1992至1993年的停火與再戰，延續至1994年7月政府軍有組織抵抗崩潰。交戰核心是總統朱韋納爾・哈比亞利馬納掌治的MRND政府及其武裝力量FAR，與在烏干達西南部結集、以盧旺達愛國陣線RPF及其愛國軍APR為主的武裝。烏干達提供營地、補給與跨境通道，但初期突入者主要是RPF戰鬥人員，不能把整支先頭部隊等同於烏干達正規軍。法國在1990年10月4日直接派兵，1994年2月又派遣外籍兵團支援哈比亞利馬納政府；比利時提供軍事顧問與裝備，協助FAR建立炮兵及後勤體系；當時的扎伊爾則提供或允許西部空運、陸路與燃料通道。法國的直接介入集中在關鍵時刻，而比利時與扎伊爾主要提供顧問、裝備及後勤便利，三者的作用並不相同。
countriesEn: The war began in northern Rwanda on 1 October 1990, passed through a border war of attrition in 1991 and renewed fighting during the ceasefires of 1992 and 1993, and continued until the organized resistance of government forces collapsed in July 1994. The principal antagonists were President Juvénal Habyarimana’s MRND government and its armed force, the Forces Armées Rwandaises, or FAR, against the Rwandan Patriotic Front, or RPF, and its Rwandan Patriotic Army, the APR, based in southwestern Uganda. Uganda provided bases, supplies and a cross-border corridor, although the initial assault force consisted principally of RPF fighters rather than regular Ugandan troops. France deployed troops directly on 4 October 1990 and sent Foreign Legion personnel again in February 1994 to support Habyarimana’s government. Belgium supplied military advisers and equipment that helped the FAR organize its artillery and logistics, while Zaire, then the name of the western neighbor, permitted or facilitated air corridors, overland movement and fuel deliveries. France’s direct intervention was concentrated at decisive moments, whereas Belgium and Zaire mainly provided advice, equipment and logistical access; their roles were therefore not equivalent.
people: 哈比亞利馬納既是總統，也是FAR最高政治指揮者，1990年的反擊、1993年的再戰及1994年的最後部署都受其 Decisions 支配。RPF首任主席兼戰地指揮者弗雷德・魯維吉瑪在1990年率領突擊；他於1991年初在北部戰線陣亡後，保羅・卡加梅以愛國軍實際指揮者身份接掌作戰，後來成為RPF主席及最終攻勢的策劃中心。政府軍方面，總統警衛隊指揮官泰奧內斯特・巴戈索拉在1993至1994年間掌握首都防衛與政府的武裝應變，FAR各師、旅及地方守備單位則依既定指揮鏈作戰。法國外籍兵團與比利時軍事顧問直接介入FAR的訓練、部署及火力協調；1993年10月成立的聯合國盧旺達支援團由雅克－羅熱・羅馬里將軍出任首任部隊指揮官，但其任務主要是觀察、聯絡與維持停火，而非替FAR承擔主要作戰。
peopleEn: Habyarimana was both president and the political head of the FAR, and his decisions shaped the counteroffensive of 1990, the renewed fighting of 1993 and the final deployments of 1994. Fred Rwigema, the first chairman of the RPF and its field commander, led the initial invasion. After he was killed on the northern front in early 1991, Paul Kagame took operational command as the leader of the APR and later became chairman of the RPF and the planner of the final offensive. On the government side, Presidential Guard commander Théoneste Bagosora directed the capital’s defenses and the government’s armed response during 1993 and 1994, while FAR divisions, brigades and local garrisons fought through their established chains of command. French Foreign Legion personnel and Belgian military advisers directly assisted FAR training, deployment and fire coordination. The United Nations Assistance Mission for Rwanda, established in October 1993, had General Jacques-Roger Romary as its first force commander. Its principal tasks were observation, liaison and monitoring the ceasefires rather than assuming the main burden of combat for the FAR.
kits: 1990年時，FAR的骨幹裝備包括FN FAL 7.62公厘步槍、Browning Hi-Power 9公厘手槍、RPG-7火箭筒、M2系列81公厘迫擊炮及M2A1 105公厘牽引榴彈炮；部分7.62×39公厘步槍、12.7公厘重機槍與火箭筒則可見於政府軍或日後繳獲的FAR武器庫。空軍編制上列有MiG-17、MiG-19戰鬥機，DHC-4 Caribou、C-47運輸機及Alouette III直昇機，可用飛機數、維修狀態與後勤供應卻限制其持續出動；總統座機則是Dassault Falcon 50。APR初期的機械化程度低，主要依靠步兵縱隊、豐田Land Cruiser 70系列車輛與普通貨車運載武器、通信組件及糧秣，後來也接收從FAR繳獲的FAL、迫擊炮、105公厘炮彈與其他軍械。7.62×39、7.62×51 NATO、9公厘與12.7公厘彈藥供應有限，81及105公厘炮彈更受運輸與道路條件約束；FAR可利用境內公路和空運補給，APR則依靠烏干達方向補給線及繳獲儲備。雙方各批次的實際庫存與逐日消耗量並無可靠完整紀錄，不能以想像數字補足。
kitsEn: At the beginning of 1990, the core equipment of the FAR included FN FAL 7.62 mm rifles, Browning Hi-Power 9 mm pistols, RPG-7 launchers, M2-series 81 mm mortars and M2A1 105 mm towed howitzers. Some 7.62×39 mm rifles, 12.7 mm heavy machine guns and rocket launchers appeared in government stocks or in FAR weapons captured later. On the air arm’s establishment were MiG-17 and MiG-19 fighters, DHC-4 Caribou and C-47 transports, and Alouette III helicopters. The number of serviceable aircraft, their maintenance state and the availability of spares limited sustained operations, while the presidential aircraft was a Dassault Falcon 50. The APR initially had low mechanization and relied on infantry columns, Toyota Land Cruiser 70-series vehicles and ordinary trucks to carry weapons, communications equipment and supplies. It later absorbed FAL rifles, mortars, 105 mm ammunition and other matériel captured from the FAR. Stocks of 7.62×39 mm, 7.62×51 mm NATO, 9 mm and 12.7 mm ammunition were limited, while the movement of 81 mm and 105 mm shells was even more constrained by transport and road conditions. The FAR could use the national road system and airlift, whereas the APR depended on supply routes through Uganda and captured depots. Reliable complete records of ammunition stocks and daily expenditure do not exist, and imagined figures should not be substituted for them.
tactics: 1990年10月1日凌晨，RPF與APR從烏干達西南部營地越過邊界，以Bunyaga一帶為主要突破口。突擊縱隊以步兵為主，車輛數量有限，先遣分隊奪取邊境哨所、通信與補給節點，再向魯亨傑里和吉塞尼方向推進；政府軍從首都調集FAR步兵，以FAL小分隊和RPG反擊，並用105公厘炮火封鎖道路與高地。10月4日，約三百名法國軍人完成空運部署，其存在與FAR本身的反擊共同迫使第一次攻勢退回北部山區。12月10日前後，APR再以多路縱隊發動攻勢，一度進入魯亨傑里與吉塞尼，並保住北部立足地。到1991年初，RPF已能固守廣大北線，而不是像最初那樣突進後立即退走。1991年的作戰轉為邊境消耗戰：APR利用魯亨傑里以北的火山高地、道路岔口與 ambush 陣地分割FAR先遣隊，政府軍則依靠首都補給線和較完整炮兵反覆奪回失地；雙方都無法在短時間內消滅對方，最終於12月29日同意停火。1992年8月31日簽訂的《阿魯沙協議》規定解除武裝、部隊駐防、整合政治力量及建立過渡政府，但執行長期停滯，1992至1993年間仍不斷出現滲透、伏擊與局部反擊。1993年10月，政府與RPF的對立再度公開化，APR沿魯亨傑里至首都方向推進，一度逼近基加利外圍；聯合國支援團主要記錄停火線與護送行動，FAR仍依靠首都道路、城防據點及外國援助維持陣地。1994年4月6日，哈比亞利馬納在吉塞尼的墜機事件中生還並返回首都；4月21日，其Falcon 50座機在起飛後遭擊中墜毀，責任歸屬從當時起即有爭議。政府高層死亡、外國援助無法立即重建FAR指揮鏈，使軍隊逐步喪失協同；4月至6月的戰鬥由政府軍據點防守與RPF局部攻勢互相拉鋸。7月1日，APR從北部、西北部及西側方向展開最後攻勢，以步兵分隊、迫擊炮與火箭筒逐段處理道路阻斷和FAR陣地，並利用FAR失守後留下的裝備補充前線。7月4日，APR進入基加利；政府崩潰後仍分散抵抗的FAR單位繼續作戰，至7月17日才失去有組織抵抗的能力。
tacticsEn: In the early hours of 1 October 1990, the RPF and APR crossed the border from their bases in southwestern Uganda, using the Bunyaga area as their principal breach. The assault columns were predominantly infantry with few vehicles. Advance detachments seized border posts, communications and supply points before pushing toward Ruhengeri and Gisenyi. The government drew FAR infantry from the capital, countered with FAL sections and RPG teams, and used 105 mm fire against roads and elevated ground. On 4 October, approximately 300 French troops completed an airlift deployment. Their presence, together with the FAR counterattack, forced the first offensive back into the northern highlands. Around 10 December, the APR launched another attack in several columns, entered Ruhengeri and Gisenyi at different points and retained a foothold in the north. By early 1991, the RPF could hold a broad northern front rather than withdraw immediately after each advance. The campaign of 1991 became a war of attrition along the border. The APR used elevated ground north of Ruhengeri, road junctions and ambush positions to divide FAR advance detachments, while government columns repeatedly retook lost ground by relying on the capital’s supply routes and fuller artillery. Neither side could destroy the other quickly, and a cease-fire was accepted on 29 December. The Arusha Accords, signed on 31 August 1992, provided for demobilization, force cantonment, political integration and a transitional government. Implementation stalled, however, and infiltration, ambushes and local counterattacks continued through 1992 and 1993. In October 1993, the confrontation between the government and RPF became openly renewed. The APR advanced along the approaches from Ruhengeri toward Kigali and at one point reached the capital’s outskirts. UNAMIR principally recorded cease-fire lines and conducted escort duties, while the FAR continued to rely on capital roads, fortified positions and foreign assistance. On 6 April 1994, Habyarimana survived the crash at Gisenyi and returned to the capital. On 21 April, his Falcon 50 was struck after takeoff and crashed; responsibility for the attack was disputed at the time and remained so. The death of senior government leaders and the inability of foreign aid to rebuild the FAR chain of command progressively destroyed coordination. Fighting between government strongpoints and local RPF attacks continued from April through June. On 1 July, the APR launched its final offensive from northern, northwestern and western approaches. Infantry sections, mortars and rocket launchers worked through roadblocks and FAR positions in stages, while captured equipment was used to support the forward forces. APR troops entered Kigali on 4 July. Dispersed FAR units continued to resist after the government collapsed, but their organized resistance ended on 17 July.
data: 可核對的時間節點包括：1990年10月1日RPF越境開戰，10月4日法國完成首次直接 deployment，12月10日前後APR發動第二次攻勢；1991年12月29日訂立停火；1992年8月31日簽署《阿魯沙協議》；1993年10月5日聯合國安全理事會第872號決議建立UNAMIR，隨後同月爆發大規模再戰；1994年2月法國再度向區內派遣地面部隊，4月6日哈比亞利馬納座機在吉塞尼墜毀但本人生還，4月21日其座機再次墜毀；7月1日APR展開總攻，7月4日進入基加利，7月17日政府軍有組織抵抗告終。公開資料常以約五千人的量級描述1990年突擊部隊，但武裝人員、訓練民兵及後勤人員是否全部計入，各方口徑不同，因此只能視為兵力規模，不能當作精確編制。FAR初期的有效作戰人數、每日傷亡與各戰役繳獲數量同樣缺乏一致紀錄，本篇不列任何未經證實的精確傷亡總數。北部多火山高地而道路有限，105公厘炮彈及機車載運的81公厘迫擊炮彈都使補給線成為進攻節奏的重要限制。
dataEn: The verifiable chronological points are: the RPF crossed the border and opened the war on 1 October 1990; France completed its first direct troop deployment on 4 October; the APR launched a second offensive around 10 December; a cease-fire was agreed on 29 December 1991; the Arusha Accords were signed on 31 August 1992; United Nations Security Council Resolution 872 established UNAMIR on 5 October 1993, followed by large-scale renewed fighting that month; France deployed ground forces again in February 1994; Habyarimana’s aircraft crashed at Gisenyi on 6 April but he survived, and his aircraft crashed again on 21 April; the APR began its general offensive on 1 July, entered Kigali on 4 July, and organized government resistance ended on 17 July. Open sources usually describe the 1990 assault force on the scale of about five thousand, but they differ over whether armed personnel, trained militia and logistics personnel were all included. The figure can therefore indicate the scale of the force but not an exact order of battle. The effective initial strength of the FAR, daily casualties and captured matériel totals also lack consistent records, so no unverified precise casualty total is provided here. Northern Rwanda offered extensive volcanic high ground but few roads, and the movement of 105 mm shells and motor-carried 81 mm mortar ammunition made supply routes an important constraint on the tempo of attack.
cause: 1990年的直接成因，是RPF在烏干達完成一定程度的組訓、補給與跨境集結後，利用哈比亞利馬納政府對北部邊境安全的憂慮發動突擊；此舉既有軍事目的，也包含要求政府改變政治與軍職分配的意思。更深層的背景是1970年代以來MRND一黨化、軍隊指揮集中，以及族群身分與軍職資源分配失衡。RPF以在烏干達的盧旺達武裝人員為骨幹，在烏干達內戰環境中獲得較長期的訓練與武器供應，FAR則得到比利時顧問及法國援助維持裝備與專業指揮。最初的邊境攻勢雖被擊退，RPF仍保住北部陣地，使衝突由一次突襲轉為長期戰爭。1991年停火與1992年《阿魯沙協議》本可建立部隊重新編組及過渡政治架構，但執行不完整，軍隊駐防、解除武裝與指揮權安排持續爭議。1993年10月再戰後，1994年的政治危機及哈比亞利馬納座機被擊落，使原本已缺乏凝聚力的FAR指揮中樞更難維持，APR因而得以把邊境戰爭轉為奪取首都與全國政權的總攻。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the 1990 war was the RPF’s completion of organization, training and supply arrangements in Uganda, followed by an invasion that exploited Habyarimana’s government’s concern about security along the northern frontier. The operation had a military purpose but also carried demands for political and military-administrative change. The deeper background included the one-party concentration of the MRND since the 1970s, centralized military command and imbalances in the distribution of military posts according to ethnic identity. The RPF was based on armed Rwandan personnel in Uganda and received extended training and weapons within the conditions created by Uganda’s civil war. The FAR, meanwhile, maintained its equipment and professional command system through Belgian advisers and French assistance. Although the first border offensive was defeated, the RPF retained positions in the north, turning an invasion into a prolonged war. The 1991 cease-fire and the 1992 Arusha Accords could have established a framework for reorganizing forces and transitional politics, but implementation was incomplete, and disputes continued over cantonment, demobilization and the distribution of command. After renewed fighting in October 1993, the political crisis of 1994 and the loss of Habyarimana’s aircraft further weakened a FAR command structure that was already losing cohesion, allowing the APR to transform the border war into a general offensive for the capital and national authority.
impact: 軍事上，這場戰爭首先改變了雙方力量結構。APR由一支以跨境突擊為主的武裝，發展為能控制北部陣地、維持多個方向攻勢並接管FAR裝備的正規化軍隊；FAR則由享有首都、公路網、空軍與外國援助的一方，逐步失去北部補給點和戰術主動權。105公厘炮兵及外國顧問在1990至1991年的反擊中重要，但無法彌平FAR在基層訓練、指揮連續性及後勤上的弱點。外交上，法國的直接出兵只延緩而不能扭轉第一次攻勢，1994年的再部署同樣未能重建政府軍；UNAMIR則證明觀察團能記錄停火與協助聯絡，卻不能替代雙方建立有效指揮。1992年的《阿魯沙協議》、1993年的政治安排及其後形成的軍事僵局，均被1994年的政權崩潰和APR總攻取代。最後，RPF不再只是依賴烏干達基地的邊境武裝，而把作戰重心轉入盧旺達境內並以奪取國家權力為目標，FAR則從全面進攻者轉為守備殘餘據點的一方。
impactEn: Militarily, the war changed the balance between the two sides. The APR developed from an organization built around cross-border incursions into a regularized force capable of holding northern positions, sustaining attacks on several axes and taking over FAR equipment. The FAR, initially possessing the capital, road network, air force and foreign assistance, progressively lost northern supply points and tactical initiative. The 105 mm artillery and foreign advisers were important during the counteroffensive of 1990 and 1991, but they could not compensate for weaknesses in FAR junior-unit training, continuity of command and logistics. Diplomatically, direct French intervention delayed rather than reversed the first offensive, and the renewed deployment of 1994 likewise failed to reconstruct the government army. UNAMIR demonstrated that an observer mission could record ceasefires and assist liaison but could not substitute for effective command on either side. The Arusha Accords of 1992, the political arrangements of 1993 and the military stalemate that followed were all overtaken by the collapse of the government and the APR’s general offensive. The RPF was no longer simply a border force dependent on bases in Uganda; it shifted the center of operations inside Rwanda and made the acquisition of state power its objective, while the FAR shifted from general attack to the defense of a diminishing number of strongpoints.
result: 軍事結果是APR取得決定性勝利。7月1日總攻開始後，FAR的指揮與補給逐步瓦解，APR於7月4日控制基加利；仍分散作戰的政府軍單位持續抵抗，至7月17日才失去有組織戰鬥能力。哈比亞利馬納的MRND政府及以他為中心的政治軍事領導就此終止，APR接管國家權力與FAR留下的大部分火炮、運輸車輛、武器及彈藥，並把愛國軍擴展為新政府的核心軍事力量。這並不是1990年10月第一次突擊立即取得的結果：那次攻勢確實被FAR與法國援助下的反擊壓回，但RPF保住北部立足點，之後經邊境消耗戰、協議階段的局部交火、1993年再戰及1994年總攻逐漸取得主動權。戰爭終點可以明確界定為政府軍有組織抵抗於7月17日基本終止，而不是宣稱所有非正規武裝活動在同一天完全消失；本篇亦不以缺乏一致憑證的傷亡數字包裝勝負。
resultEn: The military result was a decisive APR victory. Once the general offensive began on 1 July, FAR command and supply progressively disintegrated, and the APR took control of Kigali on 4 July. Government units that continued to fight in dispersed formations maintained their resistance until 17 July, when their organized combat capability ended. Habyarimana’s MRND government and the political-military leadership centered on him ceased to exist, while the APR assumed state power and most of the artillery, transport vehicles, weapons and ammunition left by the FAR. It expanded the APR into the core military force of the new government. This was not an immediate result of the first invasion attempt in October 1990. That offensive was pushed back by the FAR with French assistance, but the RPF retained its northern foothold and subsequently gained the initiative through a border war of attrition, intermittent fighting during the implementation of the agreements, renewed war in 1993 and the general offensive of 1994. The war’s military endpoint can be defined as the effective end of organized government resistance on 17 July, without claiming that every irregular armed activity disappeared on the same day. Nor should the outcome be presented through casualty figures for which consistent evidence is unavailable.
